newsitem.title: UK: SOCCCER-COVENTRY ESCAPE AS MIDDLESBROUGH, SUNDERLAND RELEGATED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCCER-COVENTRY ESCAPE AS MIDDLESBROUGH, SUNDERLAND RELEGATED.

text.p: Big-spending F.A. Cup finalists Middlesbrough and their North-East neighbours Sunderland crashed out of the English premier league while Coventry staged another dramatic escape on Sunday.
As Middlesbrough and Sunderland joined already-doomed Nottingham Forest in the first division next season, Coventry escaped relegation after winning 2-1 at Tottenham.
First-half goals from Dion Dublin and Paul Williams saved them-- the 10th time in 30 years they have avoided the drop on the last day of the season.
Middlesbrough's chairman Steve Gibson said: "There are highs and lows in football, and this is definitley a low. We have the cup final next week and hopefuly we will win that."
Sunderland manager Peter Reid said: "It's not the end of the world to be relegated to the first division, it just feels like it is."

There was an agonizing wait for Sunderland's fans because Coventry's match at Tottenham kicked off 15 minutes after all the other games started, due to traffic congestion around Tottenham's White Hart Lane ground.
With Sunderland's match already over, if Tottenham had forced a draw in the final 15 minutes, Coventry could still have been relegated.

Coventry player-manager Gordon Strachan said: "The players today played with as much heart as any world class players I have been lucky to play with in my career. Some of their football was today was superb, considering the pressure they were under."

Middlesbrough, with Brazilian Juninho scoring his 15th goal of the season, could only draw 1-1 at Leeds, while Sunderland lost 1-0 to an 85th minute Jason Euell goal at Wimbledon to complete a bitter-sweet day for the North-East.

For while both Middlesbrough, whose manager Bryan Robson spent 16 milllion pounds ($26 million) assembling a side which included Italian Fabrizio Ravanelli, and Brazilians Juninho and Emerson, and Sunderland went down, neighbours Newcastle crushed Nottingham Forest 5-0 to finish second to Manchester United and claimed England's second European Cup place next season.

Southampton, who could also have been relegated depending on the outcome of their match at Aston Villa and results elsewhere, also avoided the drop, despite losing 1-0 at Villa Park. Defender Richard Dryden scored an own goal after only 12 minutes.
Southampton finished 16th with 41points, Coventry were 17th with 41, Sunderland 18th on 40, Middlesbrough 19th on 39 and Forest bottom with 34.
Middlesbrough would have been safe on 42 if they had not had three points deducted for failing to play a match at Blackburn last December. The club claimed too many players were ill.
Although they lost an appeal to the league to have the points re-instated, they are believed to be considering an appeal to the High Court to have that decision overturned.
If they did that, the situation regarding the relegation positions would be a matter of some uncertainty during the close season.

Chairman Gibson refused to rule out a legal challenge after the match at Leeds. "We have been relegated today not because of what happened on the football pitch but because of a decision made by grey men in grey suits behind closed doors," he said.
Asked whether a legal challenge would be made, Gibson replied: "That's for me to know. Those who deducted us three points will be the first to know my message."

Manchester United finished off their season in style. They were presented with the league trophy for the fourth time in five seasons before their final game at home against West Ham which they won 2-0. Scorers were Ole Solskjaer and Jordi Cruyff.
Liverpool, who started the day second, finished fourth after being held 1-1 by Sheffield Wednesday who had goalkeeper Matt Clarke sent off for deliberate handball.
Arsenal, who were fourth, finished third after winning 3-1 at Derby, despite having skipper Tony Adams sent off for two yellow cards in three minutes.
Ian Wright (2) and Dennis Bergkamp scored Arsenal's goals in the last match to be played at the Baseball Ground after 102 years. Derby are moving to a new stadium next season.
League Cup winners Leicester, who will be joined in the UEFA Cup next season by Arsenal, Liverpool and Aston Villa, won 4-2 at Blackburn.
F.A. Cup finalists Chelsea won 2-1 at Everton despite having Norwegian goalkeeper Frode Grodas sent off.
